# Serīsakavimānavatthu (Vv 84)

**ID:** Vv 84
**Section:** Vimānavatthu (vv)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Serīsakavimānavatthu
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0506m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Serīsakavimānavatthu* (Vv 84) is a canonical text in the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya. In this narrative, a deity named Serīsaka recounts how he arrived at his comfortable existence in the heavenly realms and advises listeners on the righteous conduct necessary to achieve a similar rebirth. Scholarly annotations note that in Pali traditions the *serīsakavimāna* designates a celestial palace situated in the realm of the Cāturmahārājika deities [Lamotte 1970]. In studies of doctrinal terminology, the text is cited alongside its *Petavatthu* twin for its use of the verbal form *adhitthahātha* ("resolutely determine") in the exhortation *dhammānuyogañca adhitthahātha* ("resolutely determine on the practice of the Dhamma") [Lim Hwee San 2009].
